resources.string: The rear deltoid arises from the scapular spine and contributes to arm movement, depending on shoulder position.
The middle fibers arise from the acromion and contribute to lifting the arm away from the body.
The front fibers arise from the lateral clavicle and help lift the upper arm forward.
The three regions converge on this bony area on the outer humerus.
Trapezius and serratus around the shoulder blade
Upper trapezius fibers connect to the lateral clavicle and help lift the shoulder girdle.
Middle fibers run toward the scapular spine and help draw and steady the shoulder blade.
Lower fibers pull on the medial scapular spine and help the blade rotate upward during elevation.
Serratus anterior follows the rib cage to the inner edge of the scapula and works with trapezius during arm elevation.
The lower tip of the scapula moves outward as the blade rotates upward.
